summary: Backend testing for Landmark Visit CRUD enhancement (iteration 10). 15/16 tests passed. Landmark visit PUT and DELETE endpoints working correctly. One bug found: PUT /api/country-visits/{id} fails with 500 error when only share_diary is updated (UnboundLocalError: has_photos not defined).

critical.issue: 500 Internal Server Error when updating only share_diary field. UnboundLocalError: 'has_photos' variable is referenced in share_diary block but only defined in photos block
critical.root_cause: In update_country_visit function, the share_diary update block (lines 274-296) references 'has_photos' variable which is only defined inside the 'if "photos" in data:' block (line 272). When share_diary is updated without photos, has_photos is undefined.

action_items: Fix UnboundLocalError in country_visits.py update_country_visit function - the leaderboard points logic in share_diary block should either be removed (share_diary doesn't affect photos) or has_photos should be initialized before conditional blocks
critical_code_review_comments: In country_visits.py line 274-296: The share_diary update block incorrectly references 'has_photos' which is only defined in the photos block. The leaderboard points logic appears to be misplaced - share_diary changes should not trigger leaderboard points recalculation, only photo changes should.

rca_of_issue.issue: PUT /api/country-visits/{id} returns 500 when updating share_diary alone
rca_of_issue.root_cause: In update_country_visit() function (country_visits.py lines 246-326), the share_diary handling block (lines 274-296) references 'has_photos' variable which is only defined inside the 'if "photos" in data:' block at line 272. When the request body contains only share_diary without photos, Python raises UnboundLocalError because has_photos was never assigned.
rca_of_issue.suggested_fix: Remove the leaderboard points logic from the share_diary block (lines 277-296) as share_diary changes should not affect leaderboard points. Alternatively, initialize has_photos at the beginning of the function using: has_photos = 'photos' in data and len(data['photos']) > 0
